Assign new documents to fitted topics

Source: R/inference.R
predict.sbert_topic_model.Rd

predict() assigns new documents to the topics of a fitted model without fitting again: it embeds the new texts (or takes their embeddings) and assigns each to the topic whose center has the highest cosine similarity with it, after scaling the centers to unit length. A fitted topic model defines its topics by their centers in the embedding space, so new texts (later responses, a held-out sample, another cohort) can be placed in the same topics, which keeps the topics and their labels fixed and makes the counts comparable across samples.

distance is one minus that similarity. A model fitted on segments splits the new texts with the same segmentation settings first and assigns each segment. The fitted model is not changed. The result is a data frame with one row per document, or per segment for a segmented model.

This rule differs from the one that formed the topics: topics() fits Lloyd's k-means, which assigns each unit to the nearest raw mean of the normalized embeddings by squared Euclidean distance, and those means are shorter than unit length by different amounts. On the units a model was fitted on, the two rules agree for almost every unit but can differ for a few units on topic boundaries, so predict() on the training texts need not reproduce the fitted topics exactly; read the fitted assignment with as.data.frame(fit, what = "documents"). For graded rather than single assignments use topic_membership(); for the topic mixture of long documents, topic_gamma().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sbert_topic_model'
predict(object, text, model = NULL, embeddings = NULL, batch_size = 32L, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model from topics().

text

Character vector of new documents.

model

A model from load_model(), a pinned model name, or NULL (default) for the default model, used to embed text; ignored when embeddings are given. Its dimension must match the fitted model.

embeddings

Numeric matrix with one row per document (one per segment for a segmented model), or NULL (default) to encode text.

batch_size

Texts per model call when encoding (default 32).

...

Unused.

Value

A base data frame with one row per document and columns document_id, document_name, text, topic, label (the fitted topic label), and distance (cosine distance to the assigned center). For a segmented model, one row per segment, with segment (position in the document) after document_name.

Conditions

sbert_dimension_mismatch when the embeddings have a different number of columns from the fitted model; sbert_bad_input when both model and embeddings are given, when embeddings has the wrong number of rows or non-finite values or a zero row, or when segmentation yields no segment; when encoding, the conditions of encode().

See also

topics() for the fit; topic_membership() for graded membership; topic_gamma() for document mixtures; representatives() for the clearest examples of each topic.

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
topic_model <- topics(corpus, n_topics = 6, column = "translation",
                      embeddings = feedback_embeddings)

# Assign three messages, giving their precomputed embeddings.
new_messages <- head(corpus, 3)
with(new_messages,
     predict(topic_model, translation,
             embeddings = head(feedback_embeddings, 3)))
#>   document_id document_name
#> 1           1              
#> 2           2              
#> 3           3              
#>                                                    text topic
#> 1                    Do you know what “one more” means?     3
#> 2 There should be two more in the red than in the blue.     4
#> 3               If it’s not a person, what could it be?     6
#>                                                         label  distance
#> 1         What does “all the ones between the leaf and the... 0.5466974
#> 2 Are you sure you have fewer pictures in the red box than... 0.2167227
#> 3    It is not a person, does not have a hat, and is sitting. 0.2611759

# A small model on toy two-dimensional embeddings.
text <- c(
  "Cats chase mice", "Dogs chase balls",
  "Stocks and bonds trade", "Markets price shares"
)
embeddings <- rbind(c(1, 0), c(0.9, 0.1), c(0, 1), c(0.1, 0.9))
toy_model <- topics(text, 2, embeddings = embeddings)
predict(toy_model, "Bulls and bears move markets",
        embeddings = rbind(c(0.2, 0.8)))
#>   document_id document_name                         text topic
#> 1           1               Bulls and bears move markets     2
#>                    label   distance
#> 1 Stocks and bonds trade 0.01792973

# \donttest{
if (interactive()) {
  predict(topic_model, c("The pictures were too small.",
                         "I liked the counting game."))
}
# }
